{"kind": "tool_result", "at": "2026-08-03T16:44:10.723139+00:00", "text": "", "tool": "Bash", "data": {"content": "\section{The admissible Abel quotient}
\label{sec:admissibleAbelQuotient}

The widened divisor representation is now unconditional. The remaining representability
argument is not an open-atlas argument: the fibres of the raw Abel map are linear systems and
can have positive dimension. Following Kleiman's proof of Theorem~4.8, the admissible divisor
scheme must instead be divided by the kernel relation of the Abel map. The following finite
dependency cone records the construction and distinguishes the landed inputs from the genuine
Altman--Kleiman quotient gate.

\begin{definition}[The represented admissible divisor source]
  \label{def:admissibleDivisorRepresentation}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.divRepAffAdmissibleParameter,
    AlgebraicGeometry.divRepAffAdmissibleScheme,
    AlgebraicGeometry.divFunctorAff_admissible_representableBy}
  \uses{def:divFamZarAff}
  \leanok
  There is a parameter \(n_{\mathrm{adm}}\), chosen from the curve data, and a scheme
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}}\) over \(\Spec k\) representing
  \(\operatorname{divFunctorAff}(C,n_{\mathrm{adm}})\), without a rational-point,
  divisor-degree, or further representability hypothesis.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The concrete admissible Abel map]
  \label{def:admissibleAbelMap}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.admissibleAbelChartIndex,
    AlgebraicGeometry.admissibleAbelChartDivisor,
    AlgebraicGeometry.admissibleAbelTrans,
    AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible_eq_sigmaExtension_admissibleAbelTrans}
  \uses{def:admissibleDivisorRepresentation, def:pic0SigmaFunctor}
  \leanok
  Choose the admissible chart index and reference divisor internally. Composing the
  representing equivalence of Definition~\ref{def:admissibleDivisorRepresentation} with
  the corresponding chart-value transformation gives a natural transformation from the
  represented divisor functor to \(\mathrm{pic}^0_{\mathrm{Set}}(C)\). Its Sigma-extension
  is the concrete map \(\operatorname{abelSigmaChartAffAdmissible}\).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The admissible source is project-local]
  \label{thm:admissibleDivisorSource_projectLocal}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.divRepAffAdmissibleEmbedding,
    AlgebraicGeometry.isClosedImmersion_divRepAffAdmissibleEmbedding,
    AlgebraicGeometry.divRepAffAdmissibleGrassmannianCover,
    AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_divRepAffAdmissibleScheme,
    AlgebraicGeometry.locallyOfFiniteType_divRepAffAdmissibleScheme,
    AlgebraicGeometry.isSeparated_divRepAffAdmissibleScheme}
  \uses{def:admissibleDivisorRepresentation, def:divScheme}
  \leanok
  The source \(D_{\mathrm{adm}}\) admits a closed immersion into a concrete pair of
  Grassmannians. Pulling back the finite affine Grassmannian cover gives a finite affine
  cover of the source; in particular the source is quasi-compact, locally of finite type,
  and separated. This is the concrete project-local input used in the quotient argument.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Kernel of the admissible Abel map]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_kernel}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.admissibleAbelTrans_app_eq_iff_forall_picClass_div_mem_picFromBase}
  \uses{def:admissibleAbelMap, def:relPic}
  \leanok
  Two admissible divisor families have the same Abel value exactly when, on every affine
  open of the test scheme, the ratio of their Picard classes lies in
  \(\mathrm{picFromBase}\). Thus the concrete kernel is precisely relative linear
  equivalence, including the quotient by classes pulled back from the base.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The admissible Abel map after big-etale sheafification]
  \label{def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subcanonical_etaleTopology,
    AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaEtaleSheafification,
    AlgebraicGeometry.admissibleAbelEtaleSourceIso,
    AlgebraicGeometry.admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}
  \uses{def:admissibleDivisorRepresentation, def:admissibleAbelMap}
  \leanok
  After raising values to the universe required by the big site and sheafifying, the
  source is identified by subcanonicity with the actual big-etale Yoneda sheaf of
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}}\). The resulting morphism has target the big-etale sheafification of
  the Sigma Picard presheaf. Identifying that target with the original Picard functor is a
  separate step.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The Sigma Picard functor is a big-etale sheaf]
  \label{thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isEtaleSheaf}
  \uses{def:pic0SigmaFunctor, thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf,
    def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}
  \notready
  The Sigma-extension of \(\mathrm{pic}^0\) satisfies descent for the big-etale topology,
  and its universe-raised sheaf is canonically isomorphic to the sheafification in
  Definition~\ref{def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Etale-local surjectivity of the admissible Abel map]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_etaleLocallySurjective}
  \uses{def:admissibleAbelMap, def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}
  \notready
  The concrete admissible Abel transformation is locally surjective for the big-etale
  topology. Equivalently, every degree-zero Picard class lifts to an admissible divisor
  family after an etale cover of the test scheme.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The sheafified Abel map is the coequalizer of its kernel pair]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_etaleCoequalizer}
  \uses{def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap,
    thm:admissibleAbel_etaleLocallySurjective}
  \notready
  Local surjectivity makes the sheafified Abel map a regular epimorphism in the category of
  type-valued big-etale sheaves. Hence it is the coequalizer of its pullback kernel pair.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The concrete Abel kernel pair is representable]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbelKernelPair_representable}
  \uses{thm:admissibleAbel_kernel, thm:admissibleDivisorSource_projectLocal}
  \notready
  Construct a scheme \(R\) representing the concrete kernel relation on
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}}\), identify it with the fibre product over the Picard sheaf, and prove
  that the first projection \(R \to D_{\mathrm{adm}}\) is smooth and proper.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The Altman--Kleiman effective quotient]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_effectiveQuotient}
  \uses{thm:admissibleDivisorSource_projectLocal,
    thm:admissibleAbelKernelPair_representable}
  \notready
  Apply the flat-proper equivalence-relation theorem to construct a scheme
  \(Q = D_{\mathrm{adm}}/R\) over \(\Spec k\), with quotient map
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}} \to Q\), and identify \(R\) with
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}} \times_Q D_{\mathrm{adm}}\). This is a construction of the concrete
  quotient, not a theorem with quotient data as a hypothesis.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Yoneda identification of the quotient]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_quotientYoneda}
  \uses{thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isEtaleSheaf,
    thm:admissibleAbel_etaleCoequalizer,
    thm:admissibleAbel_effectiveQuotient,
    thm:admissibleAbel_kernel}
  \notready
  The Yoneda sheaf of \(Q\) and the degree-zero Picard Sigma functor are coequalizers of
  the same represented kernel pair. The induced isomorphism is compatible with the
  structure maps to \(\Spec k\), and therefore descends from the Sigma-extension to
  \(\mathrm{pic}^0_{\mathrm{Set}}(C)\) on the slice.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The admissible Abel quotient representer]
  \label{def:pic0AdmissibleAbelQuotientRepresenter}
  \uses{thm:admissibleAbel_quotientYoneda, thm:representableBy_overSlice}
  \notready
  The direct endpoint is
  \[
    \operatorname{pic0AdmissibleAbelQuotientRepresenter}(C)
      : \sum_{Q : \Over(\Spec k)}
          \mathrm{RepresentableBy}\bigl(\mathrm{pic0TypeFunctor}(C),Q\bigr).
  \]
  Its body chooses the admissible datum internally, directly consumes
  \(\operatorname{divFunctorAff\_admissible\_representableBy}\), constructs the effective
  quotient above, and returns its Yoneda comparison. It has no representability,
  local-surjectivity, kernel-pair, rational-point, or quotient-data binder.
\end{definition}

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffChallenge

     8	/-!
     9	# Cohomology of admissible-degree divisors
    10	
    11	The admissible Abel parameter lies above the uniform ledger bound.  Consequently, every
    12	divisor whose degree is at least that parameter has vanishing `H^1`.  At exact admissible
    13	degree, the Riemann--Roch rank anchor then computes `h^0`, and hence the projective dimension
    14	of the corresponding complete linear system.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    19	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory
    24	
    25	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    26	
    27	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    28	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
    29	
    30	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    31	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    32	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    33	variable (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    34	
    35	local instance instIsIntegralRelCurveKernelFibre :
    36	    IsIntegral (relCurve C L) :=
    37	  instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
    38	
    39	local instance instSmoothRelCurveKernelFibre :
    40	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
    41	  instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
    42	
    43	local instance instQuasiCompactRelCurveKernelFibre :
    44	    QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
    45	  instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
    46	
    47	local instance instModuleFiniteH0RelCurveKernelFibre :
    48	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
    49	  instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
    50	
    51	local instance instModuleFiniteH1RelCurveKernelFibre :
    52	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
    53	  instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
    54	
    55	/-- Divisors of degree at least the admissible Abel parameter have vanishing first
    56	cohomology.  The statement is monotone in the degree, so exact admissible degree is a direct
    57	special case rather than an additional hypothesis. -/
    58	theorem subsingleton_h1_of_divRepAffAdmissibleParameter_le_deg
    59	    (D : (relCurve C L).CurveDivisor)
    60	    (hD : (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ) ≤
    61	      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D) :
    62	    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).divisorSheaf L D) 1) := by
    63	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
    64	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
    65	    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
    66	  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
    67	  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
    68	    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
    69	  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
    70	    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
    71	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
    72	    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
    73	  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
    74	    moduleFinite_hModule_one C
    75	  apply subsingleton_h1_of_ledger_bound
    76	    (C := C) (π := divRepAffP1Map C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C)
    77	      (genus C) (chi_moduleKSheaf C) L D
    78	  exact (ledgerBound_le_admissibleCoverageParameter
    79	    (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) (genus C)).trans hD
    80	
    81	/-- At exact admissible degree, Riemann--Roch computes the section rank as the admissible
    82	parameter plus one minus the genus. -/
    83	theorem h0_divisorSheaf_eq_divRepAffAdmissibleParameter_add_one_sub_genus
    84	    (D : (relCurve C L).CurveDivisor)
    85	    (hD : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D =
    86	      (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ)) :
    87	    (Sheaf.h0 ((relCurve C L).divisorSheaf L D) : ℤ) =
    88	      (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ) + 1 - (genus C : ℤ) := by
    89	  have h1 :=
    90	    subsingleton_h1_of_divRepAffAdmissibleParameter_le_deg C L D hD.ge
    91	  have h0 := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := L) D h1
    92	  have hchi := chi_relCurve_baseField C L (genus C) (chi_moduleKSheaf C)
    93	  rw [hD, hchi] at h0
    94	  omega
    95	
    96	/-- The complete linear system of an admissible-degree divisor has projective dimension equal
    97	to the admissible parameter minus the genus. -/
    98	theorem h0_sub_one_eq_divRepAffAdmissibleParameter_sub_genus
    99	    (D : (relCurve C L).CurveDivisor)
   100	    (hD : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D =
   101	      (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ)) :
   102	    Sheaf.h0 ((relCurve C L).divisorSheaf L D) - 1 =
   103	      divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C - genus C := by
   104	  have h0 :=
   105	    h0_divisorSheaf_eq_divRepAffAdmissibleParameter_add_one_sub_genus C L D hD
   106	  have hg := genus_le_divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C
   107	  omega
   108	
   109	end AlgebraicGeometry

+import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffChallenge
+
+/-!
+# Cohomology of admissible-degree divisors
+
+The admissible Abel parameter lies above the uniform ledger bound.  Consequently, every
+divisor whose degree is at least that parameter has vanishing `H^1`.  At exact admissible
+degree, the Riemann--Roch rank anchor then computes `h^0`, and hence the projective dimension
+of the corresponding complete linear system.
+
+These are field-fibre calculations only.  They do not construct a universal divisor line
+bundle, prove local freeness or base change for its pushforward, or produce a relative
+projective bundle or kernel scheme.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
+set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
+
+universe u
+
+open CategoryTheory
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry
+
+attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
+attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver
+
+variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
+variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
+  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
+variable (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
+
+local instance instIsIntegralRelCurveKernelFibre :
+    IsIntegral (relCurve C L) :=
+  instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
+
+local instance instSmoothRelCurveKernelFibre :
+    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
+  instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
+
+local instance instQuasiCompactRelCurveKernelFibre :
+    QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
+  instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
+
+local instance instModuleFiniteH0RelCurveKernelFibre :
+    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
+  instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
+
+local instance instModuleFiniteH1RelCurveKernelFibre :
+    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
+  instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
+
+/-- Divisors of degree at least the admissible Abel parameter have vanishing first
+cohomology.  The statement is monotone in the degree, so exact admissible degree is a direct
+special case rather than an additional hypothesis. -/
+theorem subsingleton_h1_of_divRepAffAdmissibleParameter_le_deg
+    (D : (relCurve C L).CurveDivisor)
+    (hD : (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ) ≤
+      Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D) :
+    Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).divisorSheaf L D) 1) := by
+  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
+  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
+    inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom)
+  haveI : IsIntegral C.left := isIntegral_left_of_geometricallyReduced C
+  haveI : LocallyOfFiniteType (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
+    inferInstanceAs (LocallyOfFiniteType C.hom)
+  haveI : QuasiCompact (C.left ↘ Spec (.of k)) :=
+    inferInstanceAs (QuasiCompact C.hom)
+  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 0) :=
+    moduleFinite_hModule_zero C
+  haveI : Module.Finite k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1) :=
+    moduleFinite_hModule_one C
+  apply subsingleton_h1_of_ledger_bound
+    (C := C) (π := divRepAffP1Map C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C)
+      (genus C) (chi_moduleKSheaf C) L D
+  exact (ledgerBound_le_admissibleCoverageParameter
+    (C := C) (divRepAffP1Map_comp C) (genus C)).trans hD
+
+/-- At exact admissible degree, Riemann--Roch computes the section rank as the admissible
+parameter plus one minus the genus. -/
+theorem h0_divisorSheaf_eq_divRepAffAdmissibleParameter_add_one_sub_genus
+    (D : (relCurve C L).CurveDivisor)
+    (hD : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D =
+      (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ)) :
+    (Sheaf.h0 ((relCurve C L).divisorSheaf L D) : ℤ) =
+      (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ) + 1 - (genus C : ℤ) := by
+  have h1 :=
+    subsingleton_h1_of_divRepAffAdmissibleParameter_le_deg C L D hD.ge
+  have h0 := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := L) D h1
+  have hchi := chi_relCurve_baseField C L (genus C) (chi_moduleKSheaf C)
+  rw [hD, hchi] at h0
+  omega
+
+/-- The complete linear system of an admissible-degree divisor has projective dimension equal
+to the admissible parameter minus the genus. -/
+theorem h0_sub_one_eq_divRepAffAdmissibleParameter_sub_genus
+    (D : (relCurve C L).CurveDivisor)
+    (hD : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D =
+      (divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C : ℤ)) :
+    Sheaf.h0 ((relCurve C L).divisorSheaf L D) - 1 =
+      divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C - genus C := by
+  have h0 :=
+    h0_divisorSheaf_eq_divRepAffAdmissibleParameter_add_one_sub_genus C L D hD
+  have hg := genus_le_divRepAffAdmissibleParameter C
+  omega
+
+end AlgebraicGeometry

1. **Keystone funnel.** Every wave funnels to one keystone with a wide parallel base;
   state the *narrowest* form a consumer needs (degree-1-only vanishing beat the full

   the source before anyone proves it (the old campaign shipped three false-as-pinned
   statements; each cost runs). Counterexamples for rejected pins go in the blueprint.

   classes or explicit structure hypotheses; `sorry` never inhabits a def/instance.
4. **One pinned universal element.** `Jacobian`, `functor`, `baseChangeIso` are all
   defined through the same `RepresentableBy` datum; coherences become uniqueness.
5. **No monoidal sheaf categories; no global adele space; no general `R^i f_*` engine;
   no Quot schemes.** Each is a measured multi-week detour whose consumers have
   cheaper curve-specific substitutes.
6. **Files ≤ 500 lines; mathlib naming; blueprint chapter per Lean directory,
   1-to-1 nodes, `\leanok` only after kernel check; `\source{}` only after reading.**
7. **Verification bar**: `lake build <Module>` (kernel), then `lean_verify` axiom audit
   (`propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound` only). LSP is advisory; `lake env lean`
   is a false oracle (lakefile sets `maxSynthPendingDepth = 3`).
8. **Uniform genus.** No genus-0 fork anywhere; `J = Pic⁰` uniformly (the old draft
   deleted a weeks-long genus-0 lane).

  \uses{def:admissibleDivisorRepresentation, def:divScheme}
  \leanok
  The source \(D_{\mathrm{adm}}\) admits a closed immersion into a concrete pair of
  Grassmannians. Pulling back the finite affine Grassmannian cover gives a finite affine
  cover of the source; in particular the source is quasi-compact, locally of finite type,
  and separated. This is the concrete project-local input used in the quotient argument.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Kernel of the admissible Abel map]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_kernel}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.admissibleAbelTrans_app_eq_iff_forall_picClass_div_mem_picFromBase}
  \uses{def:admissibleAbelMap, def:relPic}
  \leanok
  Two admissible divisor families have the same Abel value exactly when, on every affine
  open of the test scheme, the ratio of their Picard classes lies in
  \(\mathrm{picFromBase}\). Thus the concrete kernel is precisely relative linear
  equivalence, including the quotient by classes pulled back from the base.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The admissible Abel map after big-etale sheafification]
  \label{def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.subcanonical_etaleTopology,
    AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaEtaleSheafification,
    AlgebraicGeometry.admissibleAbelEtaleSourceIso,
    AlgebraicGeometry.admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}
  \uses{def:admissibleDivisorRepresentation, def:admissibleAbelMap}
  \leanok
  After raising values to the universe required by the big site and sheafifying, the
  source is identified by subcanonicity with the actual big-etale Yoneda sheaf of
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}}\). The resulting morphism has target the big-etale sheafification of
  the Sigma Picard presheaf. Identifying that target with the original Picard functor is a
  separate step.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The Sigma Picard functor is a big-etale sheaf]
  \label{thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isEtaleSheaf}
  \uses{def:pic0SigmaFunctor, thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf,
    def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}
  \notready
  The Sigma-extension of \(\mathrm{pic}^0\) satisfies descent for the big-etale topology,
  and its universe-raised sheaf is canonically isomorphic to the sheafification in
  Definition~\ref{def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Etale-local surjectivity of the admissible Abel map]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_etaleLocallySurjective}
  \uses{def:admissibleAbelMap, def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap}
  \notready
  The concrete admissible Abel transformation is locally surjective for the big-etale
  topology. Equivalently, every degree-zero Picard class lifts to an admissible divisor
  family after an etale cover of the test scheme.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The sheafified Abel map is the coequalizer of its kernel pair]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_etaleCoequalizer}
  \uses{def:admissibleAbelEtaleSheafMap,
    thm:admissibleAbel_etaleLocallySurjective}
  \notready
  Local surjectivity makes the sheafified Abel map a regular epimorphism in the category of
  type-valued big-etale sheaves. Hence it is the coequalizer of its pullback kernel pair.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The concrete Abel kernel pair is representable]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbelKernelPair_representable}
  \uses{thm:admissibleAbel_kernel, thm:admissibleDivisorSource_projectLocal}
  \notready
  Construct a scheme \(R\) representing the concrete kernel relation on
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}}\), identify it with the fibre product over the Picard sheaf, and prove
  that the first projection \(R \to D_{\mathrm{adm}}\) is smooth and proper.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The Altman--Kleiman effective quotient]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_effectiveQuotient}
  \uses{thm:admissibleDivisorSource_projectLocal,
    thm:admissibleAbelKernelPair_representable}
  \notready
  Apply the flat-proper equivalence-relation theorem to construct a scheme
  \(Q = D_{\mathrm{adm}}/R\) over \(\Spec k\), with quotient map
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}} \to Q\), and identify \(R\) with
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}} \times_Q D_{\mathrm{adm}}\). This is a construction of the concrete
  quotient, not a theorem with quotient data as a hypothesis.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Yoneda identification of the quotient]
  \label{thm:admissibleAbel_quotientYoneda}
  \uses{thm:pic0SigmaFunctor_isEtaleSheaf,
    thm:admissibleAbel_etaleCoequalizer,
    thm:admissibleAbel_effectiveQuotient,
    thm:admissibleAbel_kernel}
  \notready
  The Yoneda sheaf of \(Q\) and the degree-zero Picard Sigma functor are coequalizers of
  the same represented kernel pair. The induced isomorphism is compatible with the
  structure maps to \(\Spec k\), and therefore descends from the Sigma-extension to
  \(\mathrm{pic}^0_{\mathrm{Set}}(C)\) on the slice.
  \source{kleiman-picard}
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The admissible Abel quotient representer]
  \label{def:pic0AdmissibleAbelQuotientRepresenter}
  \uses{thm:admissibleAbel_quotientYoneda, thm:representableBy_overSlice}
  \notready
  The direct endpoint is
  \[
    \operatorname{pic0AdmissibleAbelQuotientRepresenter}(C)
      : \sum_{Q : \Over(\Spec k)}
          \mathrm{RepresentableBy}\bigl(\mathrm{pic0TypeFunctor}(C),Q\bigr).
  \]
  Its body chooses the admissible datum internally, directly consumes
  \(\operatorname{divFunctorAff\_admissible\_representableBy}\), constructs the effective
  quotient above, and returns its Yoneda comparison. It has no representability,
  local-surjectivity, kernel-pair, rational-point, or quotient-data binder.
\end{definition}

Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. lean_status: lean_ok

title: Kernel after big-etale sheafification
type: tex
updated: '2026-08-04T01:01:44'
---
Equality under the sheafified Abel map is equivalent to the raw equalizer sieve being
  covering for the big-etale topology. Membership of an arrow in that sieve is equivalent
  to the pulled-back divisor classes differing by \(\mathrm{picFromBase}\) on every affine
  open. Thus the sheafified kernel is locally the same concrete relative-linear-equivalence
  relation, including the quotient by line bundles from the base.---

content_type: theorem
created: '2026-08-04T01:01:44'

label: thm:admissibleAbel_fibreRank
lean_status: lean_ok
order: 1128
title: Fibre dimension at the admissible degree
type: tex
updated: '2026-08-04T01:01:44'
---
On every field fibre, divisors of degree at least (n_{\mathrm{adm}}) have vanishing
  (H^1). At exact admissible degree their section rank is
  (n_{\mathrm{adm}}+1-g), so the numerical projective dimension of the complete linear
  system is (n_{\mathrm{adm}}-g). This is only the fibre calculation: a universal divisor
  line bundle, locally free pushforward with base change, and a relative projective bundle
  remain to be constructed.---

The concrete admissible Abel transformation is locally surjective for the big-etale
  topology. Equivalently, every degree-zero Picard class lifts to an admissible divisor

title: Fibre dimension at the admissible degree
type: tex
updated: '2026-08-04T01:01:44'
---
On every field fibre, divisors of degree at least (n_{\mathrm{adm}}) have vanishing
  (H^1). At exact admissible degree their section rank is
  (n_{\mathrm{adm}}+1-g), so the numerical projective dimension of the complete linear
  system is (n_{\mathrm{adm}}-g). This is only the fibre calculation: a universal divisor
  line bundle, locally free pushforward with base change, and a relative projective bundle
  remain to be constructed.hgraph/nodes/4f4628ea6959.md

lean_status: lean_ok
order: 1130
title: Kernel after big-etale sheafification
type: tex
updated: '2026-08-04T01:01:44'
---
Equality under the sheafified Abel map is equivalent to the raw equalizer sieve being
  covering for the big-etale topology. Membership of an arrow in that sieve is equivalent
  to the pulled-back divisor classes differing by \(\mathrm{picFromBase}\) on every affine
  open. Thus the sheafified kernel is locally the same concrete relative-linear-equivalence
  relation, including the quotient by line bundles from the base.hgraph/nodes/8059f4299950.md

type: tex

Apply the flat-proper equivalence-relation theorem to construct a scheme
  \(Q = D_{\mathrm{adm}}/R\) over \(\Spec k\), with quotient map
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}} \to Q\), and identify \(R\) with
  \(D_{\mathrm{adm}} \times_Q D_{\mathrm{adm}}\). This is a construction of the concrete
  quotient, not a theorem with quotient data as a hypothesis.hgraph/nodes/cb9fda0713e1.md

  structure maps to \(\Spec k\), and therefore descends from the Sigma-extension to
  \(\mathrm{pic}^0_{\mathrm{Set}}(C)\) on the slice.hgraph/nodes/b261b39624fd.md

content_type: definition

title: The admissible Abel quotient representer
type: tex
updated: '2026-08-04T01:01:44'
---
The direct endpoint is
  \[
    \operatorname{pic0AdmissibleAbelQuotientRepresenter}(C)
      : \sum_{Q : \Over(\Spec k)}
          \mathrm{RepresentableBy}\bigl(\mathrm{pic0TypeFunctor}(C),Q\bigr).
  \]
  Its body chooses the admissible datum internally, directly consumes
  \(\operatorname{divFunctorAff\_admissible\_representableBy}\), constructs the effective
  quotient above, and returns its Yoneda comparison. It has no representability,
  local-surjectivity, kernel-pair, rational-point, or quotient-data binder.
